summary: Missouri Conservation Commission lookout on a Jefferson County ridge; the 1968 steel tower still stands in Sunridge Park, so the brief's gone status is wrong.

facts.design: Steel tower erected in 1968 on the site of a wooden tower

staffing.status: conservation agency no longer had use for it

access.note: Jefferson County park open from dawn until dusk. The county listing does not say whether the tower can be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Park has walking trails, picnic tables, a pavilion and a playground.

events.note: Conservation Commission bought the 6.06-acre site from Roy and Milerna Yates on 16 December 1948.
First wooden tower. State records as relayed in a 2014 history give 1940; a 1968 newspaper report gives 1949.
Public dedication of the Sun Ridge Fire Tower, announced for 17 June 1951.
Forest agent Jack Koch reported four fires in one day in April 1968.
Wooden tower dismantled by early September 1968. An 80-foot steel tower was erected on the same site; a state report for FY 1968-69 confirms it.
Conservation Commission deeded the site to Jefferson County Parks, which said the state no longer had use for it.

corrections.why: The county parks page describes the old fire tower as standing on the park property, and the 2014 history found the metal tower standing there.
The conservation agency deeded the site to Jefferson County Parks in 1980. The state commission managed the tower before that, so its name stays in the history.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2014 history gives 1940 from state records, possibly built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. A 1968 newspaper report gives 1949. The record uses 1940 and the story gives both.
The 1968 construction report and St. Louis Magazine give 80 feet (24.4 m). A 2014 history estimated about 100 feet and a Leader article says 100 feet. The record keeps 24.4 m from the 1968 build.
A 2014 history says the steel tower replaced the wooden one in 1969. The 1968 newspaper report and the state FY 1968-69 annual report place it in 1968 to 1969. The record uses 1968.

notes_for_editor: The brief's gone status is wrong: the tower stands in Sunridge Park and is open dawn to dusk. The 1951 and 1968 newspaper items and the FY 1968-69 annual report are read through the Central US Lookouts page, not the originals. Build year (1940 vs 1949) and height (80 vs 100 ft) conflict across sources and are both shown. The county listing does not say whether climbing is allowed, so the story does not say.
